summary:
SELENE-COMPARE is an interactive, browser-based simulation tool that helps lunar mission planners, scientists, and the public evaluate candidate landing sites at the Moon's South Pole.
At polar latitudes, the Sun grazes the horizon at 0°–3°, Permanently Shadowed Regions reach 35 K, and Earth vanishes behind crater rims. A one-week launch delay can turn a safe site deadly. Existing tools require tedious manual queries.
SELENE-COMPARE provides real-time, side-by-side comparison of all 13 Artemis III candidate regions using a CesiumJS 3D lunar globe, multi-track Gantt timelines, schedule-slip sensitivity analysis, Monte Carlo risk assessment, and an ROI site optimizer. Three modes serve Planners (telemetry + exports), Explorers (visual verdicts), and Learners (interactive tours on polar physics).
All computations run entirely in-browser with sub-arcminute precision (< 0.05°) validated against NASA Apollo 11 telemetry and LRO/LOLA terrain data.
details:
What it does:

SELENE-COMPARE is a high-precision, rapid-decision visual simulation system for evaluating candidate lunar landing sites at the Moon's South Pole. Users select candidate sites — including all 13 official Artemis III regions (Nobile Rim 1 & 2, Haworth, Malapert Massif, Mons Mouton, Peak near Cabeus B, Shackleton Rim, Leibnitz Beta, de Gerlache Rim, Connecting Ridge, and more) — set a mission epoch window, and instantly see detailed operational viability comparisons.

How it works:

- Ephemeris Engine: Implements the IAU 2009 / Archinal et al. 2011 lunar orientation model with 13 Delaunay angles, producing sub-arcminute (< 0.05°) body-fixed Sun and Earth vectors.

- Topocentric Visibility: Computes local horizon coordinates at each site, accounting for topocentric Earth parallax (up to 0.26°) — critical when Earth grazes crater rims.

- LOLA Terrain Masks: Uses NASA LRO/LOLA Digital Elevation Models for real terrain-blocked visibility.

- Sub-second Bisection: 12-iteration binary search (0.44s precision) for exact sunrise, sunset, earthrise, and earthset timestamps.

- Monte Carlo Risk Assessment: 100+ stochastic trials to assess landing safety and thermal risk.

- ROI Site Optimizer: Draw a polygon on the 3D Moon to find the optimal landing site within it.

Key benefits:

- Replaces hours of manual JPL Horizons queries with instant visual answers.

- Schedule Slip Analysis: See how ±7-day and ±29.53-day launch delays affect every metric.

- Automated Alternatives Finder: Scans ±14 days and neighboring sites for best fallback options.

- Three user modes: Planner (telemetry + CSV/PDF export), Explorer (visual verdicts + countdowns), Learn (interactive tours on PSRs, libration, cold traps).

- Data Export: Time-series CSV, contact intervals CSV, mission summary PDF, shareable URLs.

What makes it creative:

We built a fully immersive decision environment — a 3D CesiumJS lunar globe with real-time day/night terminator, panoramic horizon skylines, polar radar sky plots, and multi-track Gantt timelines — all synchronized at 60 FPS in the browser. A real-world replanning workflow: "Launch slipped one week → Is our site still safe? → SELENE-COMPARE shows the Sun window shifted → Site B keeps 100% Earth contact → We move the landing."

What we hope to achieve:

We aim for SELENE-COMPARE to become a go-to rapid assessment tool for Artemis planning teams, CLPS commercial landers, international partners, and educators.

Tools, languages, and software:

- TypeScript, React 18, HTML5 Canvas

- CesiumJS (3D lunar globe), Three.js (3D rendering)

- astronomy-engine library (celestial computations)

- Vite (build), Tailwind CSS + Radix UI (styling)

- jsPDF (PDF export), Vitest (automated tests)

- Deployed on Vercel, source on GitHub

- Validated against NASA Apollo 11 telemetry (computed: 10.69° vs NASA: ~10.8°)
